title: Cover Picture and Issue Information
content:
A “skip” female Weddell seal in McMurdo Sound rests on the sea ice. Since she skipped having a pup this year, she doesn’t have to expend energy caring for offspring—which probably leaves her with more time to enjoy a nice snow pillow. Photo credit: Amy Kirkham. NMFS Permit #17411.

This month’s cover image is provided by the authors of ’Hormones reflect the impacts of reproductive rest on subsequent pregnancy in a marine predator’ (https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2435.70198), which features in this issue. They examined over 130 female Weddell seals to assess how a year of reproductive rest affects hormone levels, reproductive cycle timing, and chances of becoming pregnant and giving birth again. Their findings reveal that physiological differences between skip and postpartum female Weddell seals persisted long after pupping and into the next reproductive cycle and suggest that reproductive rest allows birth timing to advance the next season, helping improve reproductive fitness and maintaining a tight temporal window for birth in the Antarctic marine environment.
